title: Nidorina’s Horn May Have Atrophied for Her Babies

direction.premise: Nidorina’s head horn has atrophied, and the Pokédex thinks this may protect her babies while feeding.
direction.audiencePromise: Watch Nidorina’s horn change, then see how feeding reveals its possible purpose.
direction.openLoop: Why would a mother Pokémon need her horn to atrophy?
direction.payoff: Her horn’s atrophy may turn feeding into a safer mouth-first meal for her offspring.
direction.engagementQuestion: Would you protect babies while feeding, or keep the horn?

voice.instructions: Use a warm, curious tone with quick pacing. Stress atrophied, babies, feeding, and horn. Pause before the reveal, then make the final question sound genuinely undecided.

scenes.headline: HER HORN MAY PROTECT BABIES
scenes.narration: Her horn atrophied. Her babies may be why.
scenes.caption: HER HORN MAY BE THE CLUE

scenes.headline: THE HORN STARTS SLOWLY
scenes.narration: Her horn develops slowly, and she favors claws and biting.
scenes.caption: THE HORN ISN’T HER MAIN ATTACK

scenes.headline: THE HORN ATROPHIES
scenes.narration: Then the horn on Nidorina's head is described as atrophied.
scenes.caption: NIDORINA’S HEAD HORN ATROPHIES

scenes.headline: SO BABIES WON’T GET POKED
scenes.narration: The Pokédex says this may stop babies getting poked.
scenes.caption: THE HORN MAY PROTECT HER YOUNG

scenes.headline: SHE FEEDS MOUTH-FIRST
scenes.narration: She chews food into paste, then spits it out for her offspring.
scenes.caption: CHEWED FOOD → OFFSPRING

scenes.headline: PROTECTION OR A TRADEOFF?
scenes.narration: Would you protect babies while feeding, or keep the horn?
scenes.caption: WHICH WOULD YOU CHOOSE?
